title: Classification (Publications, Films and Computer Games) Amendment (Loot Boxes) Bill 2022
short_title: Classification (Publications, Films and Computer Games) Amendment (Loot Boxes) Bill 2022

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would change how games with purchasable mystery prizes are rated by Australia's classification system.
The Classification Board would have to give games containing these prize mechanisms a rating of R18+ or Refused Classification, and require a label warning parents about them.
The bill says loot boxes can be virtual boxes, crates, prize wheels or similar mechanisms that contain undisclosed items bought with real money.
changes: Requires the Classification Board to factor in loot boxes when deciding a game's rating.
Forces a minimum rating of R18+ or Refused Classification on any game that includes loot boxes.
Mandates a warning notice on games that contain loot boxes or similar features.
summary.affected: Producers and sellers of computer, video and online games, and parents and guardians who buy or supervise access to these games.
